analysis.evidence: גָּבְרוּ agrees with the plural subject הַמַּיִם (“the waters”). The repeated מְאֹד מְאֹד intensifies the verb, and the following clause shows how fully the waters prevailed over the earth: all the high mountains were covered.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural

analysis.evidence: The marked מְאֹד modifies גָּבְרוּ, describing how greatly the waters prevailed. The repetition מְאֹד מְאֹד intensifies that degree.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of degree, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The marked מְאֹד is the second in מְאֹד מְאֹד. The repetition intensifies גָּבְרוּ, expressing how greatly the waters prevailed over the land.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of degree, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עַל הָאָרֶץ identifies where the waters prevailed, “over the earth.” The following clause confirms the spatial sense by describing how the waters covered all the high mountains.
The waters rose עַל הָאָרֶץ, “over the earth.” The following clause describes their reach: they covered every high mountain under the whole sky.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a common noun, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: The passive plural verb agrees with its following subject, כָּל הֶהָרִים הַגְּבֹהִים, “all the high mountains.” The preceding clause identifies the rising floodwaters as what covered them.
analysis.morphology: Pual wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: כָּל modifies the definite plural הֶהָרִים הַגְּבֹהִים, “the high mountains.” The verb וַיְכֻסּוּ, “were covered,” applies to all of them.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The adjective הַגְּבֹהִים agrees with הֶהָרִים in gender, number, and definiteness. Together with כָּל they mean “all the high mountains,” which the floodwaters covered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with prefixed definite article הֶ־.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל הֶהָרִים הַגְּבֹהִים, “all the high mountains,” the adjective agrees with הֶהָרִים in gender, number, and definiteness. It describes the physical height of the mountains covered by the floodwaters.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural absolute adjective, used attributively.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the relative clause describing הֶהָרִים הַגְּבֹהִים, “the high mountains.” The phrase תַּחַת כָּל הַשָּׁמָיִם gives their location, yielding “the high mountains that were under all the heavens.”
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The relative clause אֲשֶׁר תַּחַת כָּל הַשָּׁמָיִם locates the high mountains under the whole sky. תַּחַת takes כָּל הַשָּׁמָיִם as its spatial complement.
In תַּחַת כָּל הַשָּׁמָיִם, “under the whole sky,” כָּל takes הַשָּׁמָיִם as its complement and refers to the sky in its entirety.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: תַּחַת כָּל הַשָּׁמָיִם means “under the whole sky.” The phrase locates the high mountains beneath the sky and emphasizes that the waters covered them all.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural common noun in the absolute state.
